For an integer $d\ge 1$, the $d$-level register is the complex inner-product
space $Q_d=\mathbb C^d$ with the standard pairing
$\langle z,w\rangle_{\rm root}=\sum_{j<d}z_j\overline{w_j}$, linear in the
first argument as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]] and
[[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]. Its **computational basis** is the
ordered standard basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of [[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]].
The register's alphabet is the ordered set $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$.

For $n\ge0$, the $n$-qubit register is the ordered tensor product over
$\mathbb C$ of $n$ copies of $Q_2$. Here $\otimes_{\mathbb C}$ is the algebraic
module tensor product ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),
with its complex-module structure and finite iterated/empty-product conventions
from [[thm-commutative-ring-module-structure-on-a-tensor-product]] and
[[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]. The tuple of
bit positions is ordered lexicographically, with the first wire as the most
significant position; the product-basis theorem below establishes the
corresponding elementary tensors as a basis. For $n=0$, the empty tensor
product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. This one-dimensional trivial
register is distinct from the zero vector space $\mathbb C^0$. By definition a
register has positive dimension; a zero-dimensional space may still occur as a
factor in the more general tensor-space construction below.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $m,n\in\mathbb N$. The standard finite free modules satisfy

$$R^m\otimes_RR^n\cong R^{mn},$$

with the tensor products of standard basis vectors corresponding to the standard basis indexed by $m\times n$.

If $F$ is a field and $V,W$ are finite-dimensional $F$-vector spaces, then

$$\dim_F(V\otimes_FW)=(\dim_FV)(\dim_FW).$$

Both assertions include a zero rank or zero-dimensional factor.

If $W$ is a subspace of a finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space $V$, then

$$V=W\oplus W^\perp.$$

Thus every $v\in V$ has unique vectors $w\in W$ and $z\in W^\perp$ with $v=w+z$.
Every finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space has an orthonormal basis. In dimension zero, this is the empty basis.

A linear map $T:V\to W$ ([[def-linear-map]]) between inner product spaces ([[def-inner-product-space]]) is a **linear isometry** if

$$\lVert Tv\rVert=\lVert v\rVert$$

for every $v\in V$, where the norm is the induced norm [[def-inner-product-norm]]. An invertible linear isometry from a real finite-dimensional inner product space to itself is an **orthogonal operator**; over $\mathbb C$ it is a **unitary operator**.

Equivalently, once the finite-dimensional characterisation is proved, orthogonal and unitary operators are the endomorphisms satisfying $T^*T=TT^*=I$.

derivations.claim: Since $h,k,e\ge1$, the registers $A=Q_{ke}$ and $B=Q_h$ are nonzero. By [F1] and [F3], $\dim(H\otimes A)=hke=\dim(K\otimes E\otimes B)$.

Choose an orthonormal basis $(u_i)_{i<h}$ of $H$ using [F5]. By [F2], $(u_i\otimes a_0)_{i<h}$ is orthonormal in $H\otimes A$. The complex polarization identity for the first-linear inner-product convention, $$\langle x,y\rangle=\tfrac14\bigl(\|x+y\|^2-\|x-y\|^2+i\|x+iy\|^2-i\|x-iy\|^2\bigr),$$ and the linearity and norm preservation of $V$ from [F6] give $\langle Vu_i,Vu_j\rangle=\langle u_i,u_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}$. Since $b_0$ has norm one by [F1], the product inner product [F2] makes $(Vu_i\otimes b_0)_{i<h}$ orthonormal in $K\otimes E\otimes B$. The linear map sending $u_i\otimes a_0$ to $Vu_i\otimes b_0$ is therefore an isometry between the two $h$-dimensional subspaces they span.

Let $S$ and $T$ be those two spans. By [F4], each ambient space is the orthogonal direct sum of its span and orthogonal complement. Choose orthonormal bases of $S^\perp$ and $T^\perp$ by [F5], of lengths $p$ and $q$. Concatenate each with the corresponding $h$-vector orthonormal list from step 1.2. Each concatenated list spans its ambient space by the direct-sum decomposition. It is linearly independent: a zero linear combination splits as $s+z=0$ with $s$ in the span and $z$ in its orthogonal complement, so directness gives $s=z=0$, and independence within each list makes every coefficient zero. Thus the concatenated lists are bases; by the definition of dimension, their lengths give $hke=h+p$ and $hke=h+q$ using step 1.1. Hence $p=q$, establishing equal complement dimensions and giving completed orthonormal bases of the full input and output spaces.

Map the completed input basis bijectively to the completed output basis, using the prescribed map on $(u_i\otimes a_0)$. Its linear extension is surjective and preserves inner products because it sends one orthonormal basis to another. It is the required $W$ by [F6]. Linearity gives $W(x\otimes a_0)=Vx\otimes b_0$ for all $x$. The argument uses only finite basis choices, not a choice axiom.

Write $\mathcal Q_n$ for the ordered tensor product of $n$ copies of the two-level register from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]], with $\mathcal Q_0=\mathbb C$. Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$. Each $g\in G$ has an arity $r(g)\ge1$ and a specified unitary $U_g:\mathcal Q_{r(g)}\to\mathcal Q_{r(g)}$. An operation model states which listed gates may be called and what access or cost is assigned to them; the matrix $U_g$ by itself is only the mathematical gate data.

For $n\ge0$, the circuit wire set is $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ in its displayed order and its state space is $\mathcal Q_n$. The computational basis word $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})$ is assigned slot $\operatorname{enc}_n(x)$ from [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]], so wire $0$ is the most significant bit and the empty register has its single basis vector in slot $0$.

A layer is a finite ordered list of gate occurrences whose wire supports are pairwise disjoint. A unitary circuit is a finite chronological list $L_1,\ldots,L_d$ of such layers, with $L_1$ applied first and $L_d$ last; $d=0$ is the empty circuit. Its input, output, and terminally measured wires are specified as ordered lists without repetitions in $[n]$. This syntax specifies finite data only; the semantic action of gates on the full register is defined separately.

equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is

order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

For a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional complex vector spaces
$H_k,K_k$ and complex-linear maps $T_k:H_k\to K_k$, the **tensor map**
$\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k:H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}\to
K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n-1}$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)(x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{n-1})=T_0x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes T_{n-1}x_{n-1}.$$

For $n=0$, the tensor map is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on the empty tensor
product $\mathbb C$.

Let $(T_k:H_k\to K_k)_{k<n}$ and $(S_k:K_k\to L_k)_{k<n}$ be finite ordered
families of linear maps between finite-dimensional complex inner-product
spaces. Then

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}S_k\right)\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)=\bigotimes_{k<n}(S_kT_k),\qquad \bigotimes_{k<n}I_{H_k}=I_{\otimes_{k<n}H_k},\qquad \left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)^*=\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k^*.$$

In the first formula, $S_kT_k$ means $S_k\circ T_k$. Here $I_{H_k}$ denotes
the identity map $x\mapsto x$. All adjoints use the
repository pairing, linear in the first argument. The empty tensor-map
identity is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on $\mathbb C$.

A linear map $T:V\to W$ ([[def-linear-map]]) between inner product spaces ([[def-inner-product-space]]) is a **linear isometry** if

$$\lVert Tv\rVert=\lVert v\rVert$$

for every $v\in V$, where the norm is the induced norm [[def-inner-product-norm]]. An invertible linear isometry from a real finite-dimensional inner product space to itself is an **orthogonal operator**; over $\mathbb C$ it is a **unitary operator**.

Equivalently, once the finite-dimensional characterisation is proved, orthogonal and unitary operators are the endomorphisms satisfying $T^*T=TT^*=I$.

For an endomorphism $T$ of a finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space $V$, the following are equivalent:

1. $T$ preserves norms.
2. $T$ preserves inner products.
3. $T$ sends every orthonormal basis to an orthonormal basis.
4. $T$ sends some orthonormal basis to an orthonormal basis.
5. $T^*T=I$.

Whenever these conditions hold, $T$ is invertible and $T^{-1}=T^*$, so also $TT^*=I$. The zero-dimensional case is included.

Let $V,W$ be inner product spaces ([[def-inner-product-space]]) over the same field and let $T:V\to W$ be linear ([[def-linear-map]]). An **adjoint** of $T$ is a linear map $T^*:W\to V$ such that

$$\langle Tv,w\rangle_W=\langle v,T^*w\rangle_V$$

for every $v\in V$ and $w\in W$. Existence is not part of the definition; in finite dimensions it will follow from Riesz representation.

derivations.claim: List the complement wires as $c_0<\cdots<c_{n-r-1}$. The rule $$|x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1}\rangle\mapsto |x_{w_0},\ldots,x_{w_{r-1}}\rangle\otimes |x_{c_0},\ldots,x_{c_{n-r-1}}\rangle$$ is a bijection from the computational basis of $\mathcal Q_n$ to the product basis of $\mathcal Q_r\otimes\mathcal Q_{n-r}$: the output lists each original coordinate once and records which coordinate occupies each position. Its linear extension $P_w$ sends one orthonormal basis bijectively to another, hence is unitary by [F2].

Put $T=U\otimes I_{\mathcal Q_{n-r}}$. By [F3]–[F5], $T^\dagger T=(U^\dagger U)\otimes I=I$ and $TT^\dagger=(UU^\dagger)\otimes I=I$. Thus $T^\dagger$ is a two-sided inverse, and [F6] gives $\|Tz\|^2=\langle Tz,Tz\rangle=\langle z,T^\dagger Tz\rangle=\|z\|^2$ for every $z$. Hence $T$ is unitary. Since $P_w$ is a surjective isometry by step 1.1, its inverse also preserves norms: for $y=P_wx$, $\|P_w^{-1}y\|=\|x\|=\|P_wx\|=\|y\|$. Therefore the composite $$\widetilde U_w=P_w^{-1}(U\otimes I_{\mathcal Q_{n-r}})P_w$$ is invertible and norm-preserving, hence unitary by [F5]. Its action, by the definition of $P_w$, applies $U$ to the selected factors in tuple order and leaves the complement factors fixed, as required.
The computational basis spans $\mathcal Q_n$. Any linear map with the specified action on its basis vectors is unique, so the embedding in step 2.1 is the unique one.

Thus both composites agree on this basis vector.
The computation in step 1.1 holds for every computational basis vector, which spans $\mathcal Q_n$. Therefore the two global linear maps agree on a basis and are equal, so the embedded gates commute.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space, let $K$ be a finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space, and let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty outcome set. A **finite instrument** from $H$ to $K$ is a family of complex-linear maps $\mathcal I_a:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$, one for each $a\in\Omega$, such that each $\mathcal I_a$ is completely positive ([[def-qc-completely-positive-map]]) and

$$\sum_{a\in\Omega}\operatorname{tr}_K(\mathcal I_a(X))=\operatorname{tr}_H(X)\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H).$$

For a density operator $\rho$ on $H$ (nonnegative with trace one, [[def-qc-density-operator]]), define the outcome weight $p_a(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}_K(\mathcal I_a(\rho))$. The **conditional state** for outcome $a$ is

$$\rho_a:=\begin{cases}\mathcal I_a(\rho)/p_a(\rho),&p_a(\rho)>0,\\[2pt]\bot,&p_a(\rho)=0.\end{cases}$$

Here $\bot$ is a symbol meaning that no conditional density operator is assigned; it is not a state. Positivity and normalization of the outcome weights, and density of every positive-probability conditional state, are proved in [[thm-qc-instrument-outcome-law-normalizes]] and [[thm-qc-instrument-conditional-state-is-density]].

$AB\in M_{m\times p}(F)$ whose entries are

The sum is the finite sum in the additive commutative monoid of $F$. If $n=0$,

Here $\bot$ is a symbol meaning that no conditional density operator is assigned; it is not a state. Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])

$$\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(BA).$$

For an integer $d\ge 1$, the $d$-level register is the complex inner-product
space $Q_d=\mathbb C^d$ with the standard pairing
$\langle z,w\rangle_{\rm root}=\sum_{j<d}z_j\overline{w_j}$, linear in the
first argument as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]] and
[[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]. Its **computational basis** is the
ordered standard basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of [[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]].
The register's alphabet is the ordered set $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$.

For $n\ge0$, the $n$-qubit register is the ordered tensor product over
$\mathbb C$ of $n$ copies of $Q_2$. Here $\otimes_{\mathbb C}$ is the algebraic
module tensor product ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),
with its complex-module structure and finite iterated/empty-product conventions
from [[thm-commutative-ring-module-structure-on-a-tensor-product]] and
[[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]. The tuple of
bit positions is ordered lexicographically, with the first wire as the most
significant position; the product-basis theorem below establishes the
corresponding elementary tensors as a basis. For $n=0$, the empty tensor
product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. This one-dimensional trivial
register is distinct from the zero vector space $\mathbb C^0$. By definition a
register has positive dimension; a zero-dimensional space may still occur as a
factor in the more general tensor-space construction below.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

$$P_a^*=P_a,\qquad P_a^2=P_a,\qquad P_aP_b=0\ (a\ne b),\qquad \sum_{a\in\Omega}P_a=I_H.$$

The products above are compositions, the sum is pointwise addition of endomorphisms, and $I_H$ is the identity map; these operations preserve linear maps ([[prop-linear-maps-form-a-vector-space]], [[lem-composition-and-identity-linear-maps]]). K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n-1}$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)(x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{n-1})=T_0x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes T_{n-1}x_{n-1}.$$

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space, let $K$ be a finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space, and let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty outcome set. A **finite instrument** from $H$ to $K$ is a family of complex-linear maps $\mathcal I_a:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$, one for each $a\in\Omega$, such that each $\mathcal I_a$ is completely positive ([[def-qc-completely-positive-map]]) and

$$\sum_{a\in\Omega}\operatorname{tr}_K(\mathcal I_a(X))=\operatorname{tr}_H(X)\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H).$$

For a density operator $\rho$ on $H$ (nonnegative with trace one, [[def-qc-density-operator]]), define the outcome weight $p_a(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}_K(\mathcal I_a(\rho))$. The **conditional state** for outcome $a$ is

$$\rho_a:=\begin{cases}\mathcal I_a(\rho)/p_a(\rho),&p_a(\rho)>0,\\[2pt]\bot,&p_a(\rho)=0.\end{cases}$$

Here $\bot$ is a symbol meaning that no conditional density operator is assigned; it is not a state. Positivity and normalization of the outcome weights, and density of every positive-probability conditional state, are proved in [[thm-qc-instrument-outcome-law-normalizes]] and [[thm-qc-instrument-conditional-state-is-density]].

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, fix an ordered
orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$ of $H$, and let
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ be complex-linear. The following are
equivalent: $\Phi$ is completely positive; $J_{\mathcal B}(\Phi)$ is
non-negative; and $\Phi$ has a finite Kraus representation.

Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])
complex inner-product spaces ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]),
with the root convention that
each inner product is linear in its first argument. Write $\mathcal L(H)$ for
the complex-linear endomorphisms of $H$ and $\mathcal L(H,K)$ for the
complex-linear maps from $H$ to $K$ ([[def-linear-map]]). A **finite Kraus
representation** of a complex-linear map
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ is a finite family
$(K_a)_{a\in A}\subseteq\mathcal L(H,K)$ such that

$$\Phi(X)=\sum_{a\in A}K_a X K_a^\dagger\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H),$$

where $K_a^\dagger:K\to H$ is the adjoint
([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]), which exists
uniquely in finite dimensions ([[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]]).
The composition $K_a\circ X\circ K_a^\dagger$ maps $K$ to $K$, so the sum
defines an output endomorphism for each input endomorphism $X$. The index set
$A$ may be empty; its sum is then the zero map. Zero operators are allowed in
a nonempty family.

Let $(\mathcal I_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ be a finite instrument from a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$ to a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $K$. Suppose that for every $a$ a finite Kraus family $(M_{a,j})_j$ represents $\mathcal I_a$. Then
$$\sum_{a\in\Omega}\sum_j M_{a,j}^\dagger M_{a,j}=I_H.$$

Let $V,W$ be inner product spaces ([[def-inner-product-space]]) over the same field and let $T:V\to W$ be linear ([[def-linear-map]]). An **adjoint** of $T$ is a linear map $T^*:W\to V$ such that

$$\langle Tv,w\rangle_W=\langle v,T^*w\rangle_V$$

for every $v\in V$ and $w\in W$. Existence is not part of the definition; in finite dimensions it will follow from Riesz representation.

For compatible linear maps between finite-dimensional real or complex inner product spaces,

$$(S+T)^*=S^*+T^*,\qquad (\lambda T)^*=\overline\lambda T^*,\qquad (ST)^*=T^*S^*,\qquad T^{**}=T.$$

Also $I^*=I$ and $0^*=0$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space and let
$T:V\to V$ be linear. The operator $T$ is **non-negative** when $T$ is
self-adjoint in the sense of [[def-self-adjoint-and-normal-endomorphism]] and

$$\langle Tv,v\rangle\ge 0$$

for every $v\in V$.

The operator $T$ is **positive** when $T$ is self-adjoint and

$$\langle Tv,v\rangle>0$$

for every nonzero $v\in V$.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, and let $I_H:H\to H$ denote the identity map $x\mapsto x$. An **effect** on $H$ is an endomorphism $E$ such that both $E$ and $I_H-E$ are non-negative in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. A **finite complete positive family** is a nonempty finite list $(E_1,\ldots,E_n)$ of non-negative endomorphisms with $\sum_{a=1}^n E_a=I_H$. The next lemma proves that every member of such a family is an effect, so the family is a finite complete effect family. This is algebraic data only; it does not assert a measurement law.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space; the pairing is linear in its first argument ([[def-dimension]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Write $\mathcal L(H)$ for its complex-linear endomorphisms ([[def-vector-space-of-linear-maps]]) and let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty outcome set. A **finite POVM** on $H$ with outcomes $\Omega$ is a family $E=(E_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ with each $E_a$ nonnegative and $\sum_{a\in\Omega}E_a=I_H$; after any enumeration of $\Omega$, these operators form the finite complete positive family of [[def-qc-finite-positive-effect-family]]. Reordering does not alter the finite sum. The complete-family lemma [[lem-qc-complete-effect-family-members-are-effects]] shows that every $E_a$ also has nonnegative complement $I_H-E_a$, so each is an effect.

For a density operator $\rho$ on $H$ (a nonnegative operator of trace one, [[def-qc-density-operator]]), its **POVM outcome weights** are

$$p_\rho(a):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_a),\qquad a\in\Omega.$$

Here $\operatorname{tr}$ is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]).

The positivity and normalization of these weights are proved in [[thm-qc-povm-probabilities-normalize]]. A POVM specifies this outcome law; it does not by itself prescribe a conditional output state.

For every natural $n$, the map
$\operatorname{tr}:M_n(F)\to F$ is linear:

$$\operatorname{tr}(A+B)=\operatorname{tr}(A)+\operatorname{tr}(B),\qquad \operatorname{tr}(\lambda A)=\lambda\operatorname{tr}(A).$$

For $A\in M_{m\times n}(F)$ and $B\in M_{n\times m}(F)$,

$$\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(BA).$$

The two products may have different sizes, and the equality includes $m=0$ or
$n=0$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector space. If $D:V\to V$ is linear
and $\operatorname{tr}(D\circ A)=0$ for every linear map $A:V\to V$, then $D=0$.
Equivalently, the trace pairing $(D,A)\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(D\circ A)$
has the property that its only first input pairing to zero with every second
input is $D=0$. This includes the zero space.

derivations.claim: For each $a\in\Omega$, [F1] makes $\mathcal I_a$ completely positive, so [F2] supplies a finite family $(M_{a,j})_j$ representing it as in [F3]. If the supplied family is empty, append one zero operator; this preserves the formula and makes each index list nonempty. Since $\Omega$ is finite, the lists can be selected one at a time by finite induction; no arbitrary-index choice is used.

Define $\Phi=\sum_{a\in\Omega}\mathcal I_a$. Concatenating the finite lists in step 1.1 gives a Kraus representation of $\Phi$. These are exactly the finite branch Kraus families of the instrument in [F1], so [F4] gives $\sum_{a,j}M_{a,j}^\dagger M_{a,j}=I_H$.

For each outcome define $E_a=\sum_jM_{a,j}^\dagger M_{a,j}$. By [F5], each summand is self-adjoint and $\langle M_{a,j}^\dagger M_{a,j}x,x\rangle=\langle M_{a,j}x,M_{a,j}x\rangle\ge0$. Thus each $E_a$ is non-negative by [F6]. Step 2.1 gives $\sum_aE_a=I_H$, so $(E_a)$ is a finite POVM by [F7].

For every $X\in\mathcal L(H)$, the Kraus formula [F3], trace linearity, and rectangular cyclicity [F8] give $\operatorname{tr}_K(\mathcal I_a(X)) =\sum_j\operatorname{tr}_K(M_{a,j}XM_{a,j}^\dagger) =\sum_j\operatorname{tr}_H(XM_{a,j}^\dagger M_{a,j}) =\operatorname{tr}_H(XE_a)$. This proves the displayed outcome-law identity for every density operator as well.

If another family $E'_a$ has the same identity for every $X$, then $\operatorname{tr}_H(X(E_a-E'_a))=0$ for all $X$. By [F8], this equals $\operatorname{tr}_H((E_a-E'_a)X)$; [F9] implies $E_a-E'_a=0$. This holds for each $a$, so the induced POVM is unique.

For an integer $d\ge 1$, the $d$-level register is the complex inner-product
space $Q_d=\mathbb C^d$ with the standard pairing
$\langle z,w\rangle_{\rm root}=\sum_{j<d}z_j\overline{w_j}$, linear in the
first argument as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]] and
[[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]. Its **computational basis** is the
ordered standard basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of [[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]].
The register's alphabet is the ordered set $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$.

For $n\ge0$, the $n$-qubit register is the ordered tensor product over
$\mathbb C$ of $n$ copies of $Q_2$. Here $\otimes_{\mathbb C}$ is the algebraic
module tensor product ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),
with its complex-module structure and finite iterated/empty-product conventions
from [[thm-commutative-ring-module-structure-on-a-tensor-product]] and
[[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]. The tuple of
bit positions is ordered lexicographically, with the first wire as the most
significant position; the product-basis theorem below establishes the
corresponding elementary tensors as a basis. For $n=0$, the empty tensor
product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. This one-dimensional trivial
register is distinct from the zero vector space $\mathbb C^0$. By definition a
register has positive dimension; a zero-dimensional space may still occur as a
factor in the more general tensor-space construction below.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

Let $C=\mathbb C^2$ be a control qubit with ordered orthonormal basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$, let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, and let $U:H\to H$ be unitary. On the control-first register $C\otimes H$, define

$$C(U):=\begin{pmatrix}I_H&0\\0&U\end{pmatrix}.$$

Thus $C(U)(|0\rangle\otimes v)=|0\rangle\otimes v$ and $C(U)(|1\rangle\otimes v)=|1\rangle\otimes Uv$. **Controlled access** means that the chosen operation model explicitly grants a call to this block operator. An ordinary call to a black-box $U$ does not silently grant a controlled call, and no query or gate cost is assigned unless the model states it.

Write $\mathcal Q_n$ for the ordered tensor product of $n$ copies of the two-level register from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]], with $\mathcal Q_0=\mathbb C$. Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$. Each $g\in G$ has an arity $r(g)\ge1$ and a specified unitary $U_g:\mathcal Q_{r(g)}\to\mathcal Q_{r(g)}$. An operation model states which listed gates may be called and what access or cost is assigned to them; the matrix $U_g$ by itself is only the mathematical gate data.

For $n\ge0$, the circuit wire set is $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ in its displayed order and its state space is $\mathcal Q_n$. The computational basis word $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})$ is assigned slot $\operatorname{enc}_n(x)$ from [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]], so wire $0$ is the most significant bit and the empty register has its single basis vector in slot $0$.

A gate occurrence on the $n$ wires is a pair $(g,(w_0,\ldots,w_{r(g)-1}))$ with distinct wire labels $w_j\in[n]$; the tuple order is the input and output factor order of the local gate. A layer is a finite ordered list of gate occurrences whose wire supports are pairwise disjoint. A unitary circuit is a finite chronological list $L_1,\ldots,L_d$ of such layers, with $L_1$ applied first and $L_d$ last; $d=0$ is the empty circuit. Its input, output, and terminally measured wires are specified as ordered lists without repetitions in $[n]$. This syntax specifies finite data only; the semantic action of gates on the full register is defined separately.

Let $C=\mathbb C^2$ be a control qubit with ordered orthonormal basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$, let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, and let $U:H\to H$ be unitary. On the control-first register $C\otimes H$, define

$$C(U):=\begin{pmatrix}I_H&0\\0&U\end{pmatrix}.$$

Thus $C(U)(|0\rangle\otimes v)=|0\rangle\otimes v$ and $C(U)(|1\rangle\otimes v)=|1\rangle\otimes Uv$. **Controlled access** means that the chosen operation model explicitly grants a call to this block operator. An ordinary call to a black-box $U$ does not silently grant a controlled call, and no query or gate cost is assigned unless the model states it.

For a finite-dimensional unitary $U$, **inverse access** is the explicitly granted operation $U^\dagger=U^{-1}$. Its availability and query or gate charge are recorded separately from forward access, including any controlled access in [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]]. For a chronological sequence of length $k\ge0$ that applies $U_1$ first and $U_k$ last, the total operator is $W=U_k\cdots U_1$ when $k>0$ and $W=I_H$ when $k=0$. For $k>0$, the inverse sequence applies $U_k^\dagger$ first, then $U_{k-1}^\dagger$, down to $U_1^\dagger$; for $k=0$ it is the empty sequence.

The empty circuit and every empty layer denote the identity on $\mathcal Q_n$.

For a finite-dimensional unitary $U$, **inverse access** is the explicitly granted operation $U^\dagger=U^{-1}$. Its availability and query or gate charge are recorded separately from forward access, including any controlled access in [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]]. For a chronological sequence of length $k\ge0$ that applies $U_1$ first and $U_k$ last, the total operator is $W=U_k\cdots U_1$ when $k>0$ and $W=I_H$ when $k=0$. For $k>0$, the inverse sequence applies $U_k^\dagger$ first, then $U_{k-1}^\dagger$, down to $U_1^\dagger$; for $k=0$ it is the empty sequence.

Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$ with maximum arity $k:=\max(\{r(g):g\in G\}\cup\{0\})$ and a circuit from [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]]. The declared **size** is the number of gate occurrences, equivalently $\sum_{t=1}^d|L_t|$; the declared **depth** is the number $d$ of explicit layers, not a minimum over alternate layerings; the **width** is the number $n$ of all wires, including workspace wires. The operation model may also assign weighted gate costs, classical bit costs, and query costs; these are separate coordinates and are summed over the calls actually made.

A workspace wire is an ancilla. A **clean-ancilla promise** specifies computational-basis zero states for the ancillas and requires their exact return for every allowed data input: if $U$ is the implemented unitary, $V_D$ is the declared data unitary, and $|0_A\rangle$ is the specified joint zero vector, then $U(x\otimes|0_A\rangle)=V_Dx\otimes|0_A\rangle$ for every allowed data vector $x$. A **dirty-ancilla promise** permits an arbitrary ancilla state independent of the data input; it may be correlated with an untouched reference. Exact dirty-ancilla restoration means the implemented unitary on data and ancillas is $V_D\otimes I_A$ on the entire joint space, where $V_D$ is the declared unitary on data. The same operator equality then holds after tensoring with the identity on any finite untouched reference. Consequently, product input between the data and the combined ancilla/reference system remains product after the operation. No uncorrelated-output claim is made for an initially data-correlated ancilla.

A controlled or inverse operation is counted only when the operation model explicitly grants that access or supplies a construction; its charge is recorded separately from an ordinary call. Inverse availability and query or gate charges are also recorded separately from controlled forward access. In particular, the matrix of $U$ alone supplies neither a controlled call nor an inverse query, in accordance with [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]] and [[def-qc-inverse-unitary-access]].

Let $(\mathcal I_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ be a finite instrument from a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$ to a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $K$. Fix an order on its finite nonempty outcome set $\Omega$, with $m=|\Omega|$. There are a common integer $r\ge1$ and Kraus families $(M_{a,j})_{0\le j<r}$, padding shorter families by zero operators, such that
$$\sum_{a\in\Omega}\sum_{j<r}M_{a,j}^\dagger M_{a,j}=I_H.$$
Let $E=Q_m\otimes Q_r$ with its ordered product basis $(e_a\otimes f_j)_{a,j}$, and define
$$Vx:=\sum_{a\in\Omega}\sum_{j<r}M_{a,j}x\otimes e_a\otimes f_j\in K\otimes E.$$
Then $V$ is a linear isometry. Let $\Pi_a$ be the projection on $E$ which keeps exactly the basis vectors $e_a\otimes f_j$. For every $X\in\mathcal L(H)$,
$$\operatorname{Tr}_E\!\left((I_K\otimes\Pi_a)VXV^\dagger(I_K\otimes\Pi_a)\right)=\mathcal I_a(X).$$
The first record register stores the observed outcome $a$; the second index $j$ is hidden environment data.

Let $H,K,E$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $V:H\to K\otimes E$ be a linear isometry. Put $h=\dim H$, $k=\dim K$, and $e=\dim E$. Let $A=Q_{ke}$ and $B=Q_h$ be the finite-level registers from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]], with first computational basis vectors $a_0$ and $b_0$. Then there is a surjective linear isometry
$$W:H\otimes A\longrightarrow K\otimes E\otimes B$$
such that $W(x\otimes a_0)=Vx\otimes b_0$ for every $x\in H$.

A measurement stage on a finite-dimensional input register is specified by a finite nonempty observed outcome set $\Omega$ and an instrument $(\mathcal I_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ as in [[def-qc-instrument-and-conditional-state]]. For an input density operator $\rho$, its unnormalized branch output is $\tau_a=\mathcal I_a(\rho)$ and its branch weight is $p_a=\operatorname{tr}(\tau_a)$. The positive weights sum to one by [[thm-qc-instrument-outcome-law-normalizes]]. The unique POVM induced by the instrument, supplied by [[thm-qc-instrument-induces-povm]], has effects $E_a$ satisfying $p_a=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_a)$. A conditional output is assigned only when $p_a>0$, using the rule in [[def-qc-instrument-and-conditional-state]]; when $p_a=0$ the value is $\bot$.

A finite classical controller may retain the observed history $a$ and select a specified finite unitary suffix $S_a$ on the quantum data. Its branch map is $X\mapsto S_a\mathcal I_a(X)S_a^\dagger$. The index $a$ is the observed outcome; any Kraus index used to represent $\mathcal I_a$ is an unobserved environment label and is not stored as classical data.

A **finite measurement history tree** for a circuit on the fixed register $D=\mathcal Q_n$ is a finite rooted tree whose internal node $h$ carries a finite nonempty outcome set $\Omega_h$ and an instrument $(\mathcal I^h_a)_{a\in\Omega_h}$ from $D$ to $D$. The edge from $h$ to its child $ha$ carries a specified finite unitary $S_{h,a}:D\to D$; its branch map is $X\mapsto S_{h,a}\mathcal I^h_a(X)S_{h,a}^\dagger$. Leaves may carry a specified finite terminal POVM on $D$. The fixed data register is the wire register of [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]]. A history is the ordered list of observed edge labels from the root; a hidden Kraus index is never included in it. Since the tree is finite and each node has finitely many children, every history and every sum over histories below is finite.

For a coherent representation, order $\Omega$ and use the computational basis $(e_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ of the finite label register $Q_{|\Omega|}$. On the orthogonal decomposition $Q_{|\Omega|}\otimes K=\bigoplus_{a\in\Omega}(\operatorname{span}\{e_a\}\otimes K)$, define the mathematical block operator by
$$B\!\left(\sum_{a\in\Omega} e_a\otimes x_a\right):=\sum_{a\in\Omega}e_a\otimes S_ax_a.$$
Its control availability is part of the operation model. In the one-bit case, [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]] specifies the exact access meaning of $C(U)$; an ordinary black-box call to $U$ does not grant a controlled call. For larger outcome sets the displayed block gate is likewise an explicit operation, or must be constructed and charged by the chosen model. No gate-set implementation or efficiency bound is part of this definition. A finite history tree is interpreted by applying this definition at each node.

Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and write $\mathcal L(H)$ and $\mathcal L(K)$ for their vector spaces of complex-linear endomorphisms with pointwise operations ([[def-dimension]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]], [[def-vector-space-of-linear-maps]], [[prop-linear-maps-form-a-vector-space]]). Let $\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ be complex-linear. For each integer $r\ge1$, put $R=\mathbb C^r$ with its standard ordered register basis ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]). Write an operator $X\in\mathcal L(H\otimes R)$ in its unique $r\times r$ block form $X=[X_{ij}]$ with $X_{ij}\in\mathcal L(H)$, and define $\Phi^{(r)}(X)$ to have blocks $[\Phi(X_{ij})]$ on $K\otimes R$. Lemma [[lem-qc-finite-ancilla-amplification-is-block-map]] proves that this block rule defines a linear map on the full operator space for every finite $r$. For $r=1$, the extension is $\Phi$ under the canonical unitary identifications $x\mapsto x\otimes e_0$ and $y\mapsto y\otimes e_0$ proved in that lemma.

The map $\Phi$ is **completely positive** if, for every finite $r\ge1$, $\Phi^{(r)}$ sends every nonnegative operator on $H\otimes R$ to a nonnegative operator on $K\otimes R$ ([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]). The quantifier includes $r=1$; complete positivity therefore implies positivity. No Kraus, Choi, or Stinespring characterization is part of this definition.

Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])
complex inner-product spaces ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]),
with the root convention that
each inner product is linear in its first argument. Write $\mathcal L(H)$ for
the complex-linear endomorphisms of $H$ and $\mathcal L(H,K)$ for the
complex-linear maps from $H$ to $K$ ([[def-linear-map]]). A **finite Kraus
representation** of a complex-linear map
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ is a finite family
$(K_a)_{a\in A}\subseteq\mathcal L(H,K)$ such that

$$\Phi(X)=\sum_{a\in A}K_a X K_a^\dagger\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H),$$

where $K_a^\dagger:K\to H$ is the adjoint
([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]), which exists
uniquely in finite dimensions ([[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]]).
The composition $K_a\circ X\circ K_a^\dagger$ maps $K$ to $K$, so the sum
defines an output endomorphism for each input endomorphism $X$. The index set
$A$ may be empty; its sum is then the zero map. Zero operators are allowed in
a nonempty family.

For a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional complex vector spaces
$H_k,K_k$ and complex-linear maps $T_k:H_k\to K_k$, the **tensor map**
$\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k:H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}\to
K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n-1}$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)(x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{n-1})=T_0x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes T_{n-1}x_{n-1}.$$

For $n=0$, the tensor map is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on the empty tensor
product $\mathbb C$.

Let $(T_k:H_k\to K_k)_{k<n}$ and $(S_k:K_k\to L_k)_{k<n}$ be finite ordered
families of linear maps between finite-dimensional complex inner-product
spaces. Then

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}S_k\right)\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)=\bigotimes_{k<n}(S_kT_k),\qquad \bigotimes_{k<n}I_{H_k}=I_{\otimes_{k<n}H_k},\qquad \left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)^*=\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k^*.$$

In the first formula, $S_kT_k$ means $S_k\circ T_k$. Here $I_{H_k}$ denotes
the identity map $x\mapsto x$. All adjoints use the
repository pairing, linear in the first argument. The empty tensor-map
identity is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on $\mathbb C$.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

For a complex vector space $H$, write $\operatorname{End}(H)$ for the set of
linear maps $H\to H$ ([[def-linear-map]]).

Let $H_A,H_B$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces with fixed
ordered orthonormal bases $(e_i)_{i<a}$ and $(f_j)_{j<b}$, respectively. The
ordered product basis of $H_A\otimes H_B$ has the $A$ index first. For
$R\in\operatorname{End}(H_A\otimes H_B)$ define
$\operatorname{Tr}_B(R)\in\operatorname{End}(H_A)$ by

$$\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_B(R)\bigr)_{i i'}:=\sum_{j<b}R_{(i,j),(i',j)}.$$

Rows are output coordinates and columns are input coordinates, as in
[[def-coordinate-column-and-matrix-of-a-linear-map]]. If $b=0$, the sum is
empty and equals $0$. The notation $\operatorname{Tr}_B$ means that the second
factor is contracted; the first factor and its order are retained.

For a finite instrument $(\mathcal I_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ and input density operator $\rho$, define the unnormalized branch output $\tau_a:=\mathcal I_a(\rho)$ and probability $p_a:=\operatorname{tr}(\tau_a)$. The family $(p_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ is a probability distribution by [[thm-qc-instrument-outcome-law-normalizes]]. Its uniquely induced POVM $(E_a)$ satisfies $p_a=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_a)$ by [[thm-qc-instrument-induces-povm]] and the outcome-law definition in [[def-qc-povm-and-outcome-law]].

The conditional branch output is $\tau_a/p_a$ when $p_a>0$ and is $\bot$ when $p_a=0$, exactly as specified by [[def-qc-instrument-and-conditional-state]]. No normalized state is assigned to a zero-probability branch. A Kraus representation $\mathcal I_a(X)=\sum_jM_{a,j}XM_{a,j}^\dagger$ is only a representation of the observed branch map: $a$ is the outcome and $j$ is not an additional observed outcome.

Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $F$ ([[def-vector-space]]).

$V$ is **finite-dimensional over $F$** when it has a **finite** basis
([[def-linear-basis]], [[def-countable]]): some basis $B$ of $V$ satisfies
$B \approx n$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$ ([[def-equinumerous]]).

For such a $V$, the **dimension of $V$ over $F$**, written $\dim_F V$, is that
$n$:

$$\dim_F V \;:=\; \text{the unique } n \in \mathbb{N} \text{ such that } V \text{ has a basis } B \text{ with } B \approx n .$$

**This is well defined.** Existence of such an $n$ is the hypothesis, together
with the fact that a finite set is equinumerous with exactly one natural number
([[lem-pigeonhole]], claim 3). Uniqueness is
[[thm-any-two-finite-bases-have-the-same-size]]: two bases of $V$ with $n$ and
with $m$ elements force $n = m$. That theorem is therefore a **prerequisite** of
this definition, not a later justification of it, and it is listed in `deps`.

$V$ is **infinite-dimensional over $F$** when it is not finite-dimensional over
$F$, that is, when $V$ has **no** finite basis. No number is attached to such a
space here: the symbol $\dim_F V$ is defined only in the finite-dimensional case,
and the expression $\dim_F V = \infty$ is not used.

**The zero space.** $\varnothing$ is a basis of $\{0_V\}$
([[def-linear-basis]]) and $\varnothing \approx 0$, so $\{0_V\}$ is
finite-dimensional with $\dim_F \{0_V\} = 0$. Conversely a space of dimension $0$
has a basis $B \approx 0$, that is $B = \varnothing$, and then
$V = \operatorname{span}(\varnothing) = \{0_V\}$
([[def-linear-combination-and-span]]).
Every finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space has an orthonormal basis. In dimension zero, this is the empty basis.

All complex inner products in this track use the root convention: they are
linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). For vectors $x,y$ in the same
space, define the Dirac pairing by

$$\langle x|y\rangle_D:=\langle y,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}.$$

The ket $|x\rangle$ denotes the vector $x$. The bra $\langle x|$ denotes the
linear functional $z\mapsto\langle z,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}$.

For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H,K$, vectors $y\in H$ and
$x\in K$, define the rank-one linear map

$$|x\rangle\langle y|:H\to K,\qquad z\mapsto\langle z,y\rangle_{H,\mathrm{root}}x.$$

Given ordered orthonormal bases of $H$ and $K$, its coordinate matrix is
$[x][y]^\dagger$, where $[x]$ and $[y]$ are the corresponding coordinate
columns and $M^\dagger:=\overline M^{\mathsf T}$ is the conjugate transpose.
The coordinate assertion is established in
[[thm-qc-dirac-notation-coordinate-identity]].

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let $K$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, and suppose a finite instrument $(\mathcal I_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ from $H$ to $K$ exists. Then $K$ is nonzero.

the register $Q_d$ from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]] is an

By [F2], pad the input by a finite clean register and extend $V$ to a surjective isometry $W$ satisfying $W(x\otimes a_0)=Vx\otimes b_0$.

Reorder $K\otimes E$ so the observed label register is first, followed by $K$, the hidden register, and the padding register; this is the canonical basis permutation of [F7]. Apply the block operation from [F3] on the observed label and $K$, acting identically on the hidden register, padding register, and reference, then undo the permutation. On the label-$a$ subspace this applies $S_a$ and leaves the two environment registers unchanged.

Let $Jx=x\otimes a_0$ be the input-padding inclusion. Checking on each elementary vector $x\otimes r$ gives $(W\otimes I_R)(J\otimes I_R)(x\otimes r)=Vx\otimes b_0\otimes r$; these vectors span, and [F6] makes the tensor extensions well-defined. Hence the inclusion maps agree on all vectors, and conjugating any operator $X$ by them gives the corresponding equality of extended output operators. This remains true for vectors and operators entangled across $H$ and $R$.

Put $r=\dim R$. If $r=0$, [F10] gives $R=0$, hence $X=0$ and the amplification identity is immediate. Otherwise choose an ordered orthonormal basis $(c_k)_{k<r}$ of $R$ by [F10] and use it to identify the reference with $\mathbb C^r$. Write $X=[X_{kl}]$ in blocks. By [F4], block $(k,l)$ of $\mathcal I_a^{(R)}(X)$ is $\mathcal I_a(X_{kl})=\sum_jM_{a,j}X_{kl}M_{a,j}^\dagger$ by [F5]. By [F6], the same is block $(k,l)$ of $\sum_j(M_{a,j}\otimes I_R)X(M_{a,j}^\dagger\otimes I_R)$. Equality of all blocks proves this finite-Kraus formula for every $X$.

For each $a$, the observed-label projection keeps only the terms with label $a$ in the coherent isometry. Retain that label and take the partial trace [F8] only over the hidden Kraus register and the padding register; the trace keeps equal hidden indices $j$, and [F13] gives $\langle b_0,b_0\rangle=1$ for the returned padding. The label factor is $|e_a\rangle\langle e_a|$ by [F11]. Thus, after canonical factor permutation, the label-resolved branch operator is $$\left(\sum_j(S_aM_{a,j}\otimes I_R)X(S_aM_{a,j}\otimes I_R)^\dagger\right)\otimes|e_a\rangle\langle e_a| =(S_a\otimes I_R)\mathcal I_a^{(R)}(X)(S_a^\dagger\otimes I_R)\otimes|e_a\rangle\langle e_a|.$$ This equals $\mathcal J_a^{(R)}(X)\otimes|e_a\rangle\langle e_a|$ by step 2.1 and step 2.2 and [F6]. Taking the partial trace of the label factor gives exactly $\mathcal J_a^{(R)}(X)$ because $e_a$ is unit by [F13].

Taking traces of equal branch operators gives the same outcome probabilities. Division gives the same conditional operator only when the shared branch weight is positive; when it is zero both descriptions assign $\bot$ by [F9]. Equality for arbitrary $X$ on $H\otimes R$ preserves all reference correlations. The finite-dimensional operator construction asserts no additional implementation or cost.

A measurement stage on a finite-dimensional input register is specified by a finite nonempty observed outcome set $\Omega$ and an instrument $(\mathcal I_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ as in [[def-qc-instrument-and-conditional-state]]. For an input density operator $\rho$, its unnormalized branch output is $\tau_a=\mathcal I_a(\rho)$ and its branch weight is $p_a=\operatorname{tr}(\tau_a)$. The positive weights sum to one by [[thm-qc-instrument-outcome-law-normalizes]]. The unique POVM induced by the instrument, supplied by [[thm-qc-instrument-induces-povm]], has effects $E_a$ satisfying $p_a=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_a)$. A conditional output is assigned only when $p_a>0$, using the rule in [[def-qc-instrument-and-conditional-state]]; when $p_a=0$ the value is $\bot$.

A finite classical controller may retain the observed history $a$ and select a specified finite unitary suffix $S_a$ on the quantum data. Its branch map is $X\mapsto S_a\mathcal I_a(X)S_a^\dagger$. The index $a$ is the observed outcome; any Kraus index used to represent $\mathcal I_a$ is an unobserved environment label and is not stored as classical data.

A **finite measurement history tree** for a circuit on the fixed register $D=\mathcal Q_n$ is a finite rooted tree whose internal node $h$ carries a finite nonempty outcome set $\Omega_h$ and an instrument $(\mathcal I^h_a)_{a\in\Omega_h}$ from $D$ to $D$. The edge from $h$ to its child $ha$ carries a specified finite unitary $S_{h,a}:D\to D$; its branch map is $X\mapsto S_{h,a}\mathcal I^h_a(X)S_{h,a}^\dagger$. Leaves may carry a specified finite terminal POVM on $D$. The fixed data register is the wire register of [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]]. A history is the ordered list of observed edge labels from the root; a hidden Kraus index is never included in it. Since the tree is finite and each node has finitely many children, every history and every sum over histories below is finite.

For a coherent representation, order $\Omega$ and use the computational basis $(e_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ of the finite label register $Q_{|\Omega|}$. On the orthogonal decomposition $Q_{|\Omega|}\otimes K=\bigoplus_{a\in\Omega}(\operatorname{span}\{e_a\}\otimes K)$, define the mathematical block operator by
$$B\!\left(\sum_{a\in\Omega} e_a\otimes x_a\right):=\sum_{a\in\Omega}e_a\otimes S_ax_a.$$
Its control availability is part of the operation model. In the one-bit case, [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]] specifies the exact access meaning of $C(U)$; an ordinary black-box call to $U$ does not grant a controlled call. For larger outcome sets the displayed block gate is likewise an explicit operation, or must be constructed and charged by the chosen model. No gate-set implementation or efficiency bound is part of this definition. A finite history tree is interpreted by applying this definition at each node.

Let $(\mathcal I_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ be a finite instrument from a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$ to a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $K$, with finite nonempty observed outcome set $\Omega$. After observing $a$, suppose the circuit applies a specified finite unitary suffix $S_a$ on $K$. For every finite-dimensional complex inner-product reference space $R$ and every input operator $X\in\mathcal L(H\otimes R)$, the measured circuit's unnormalized branch on $K\otimes R$ is
$$\mathcal J_a^{(R)}(X):=(S_a\otimes I_R)(\mathcal I_a^{(R)}(X))(S_a^\dagger\otimes I_R),$$
where, after choosing an ordered orthonormal basis of $R$, $\mathcal I_a^{(R)}$ denotes the finite ancillary block amplification on $\mathcal L(H\otimes R)$: if $X=[X_{kl}]$, then $\mathcal I_a^{(R)}(X)=[\mathcal I_a(X_{kl})]$. This is the block extension in the complete-positivity definition. The coherent construction retains the observed label register until terminal readout. Its outcome-$a$ branch, after tracing out the hidden Kraus and padding registers but retaining the label, is $\mathcal J_a^{(R)}(X)\otimes|e_a\rangle\langle e_a|$ on $K\otimes R$ and the label register (up to the canonical factor permutation); discarding the label gives the same data-reference branch map. Thus it preserves the complete outcome law and all correlations with $R$. This is an exact denotational statement: any newly used dilation or block operation must be listed and charged by a gate or oracle model; no same-alphabet synthesis or cost bound is asserted.

For a finite instrument $(\mathcal I_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ and input density operator $\rho$, define the unnormalized branch output $\tau_a:=\mathcal I_a(\rho)$ and probability $p_a:=\operatorname{tr}(\tau_a)$. The family $(p_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ is a probability distribution by [[thm-qc-instrument-outcome-law-normalizes]]. Its uniquely induced POVM $(E_a)$ satisfies $p_a=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_a)$ by [[thm-qc-instrument-induces-povm]] and the outcome-law definition in [[def-qc-povm-and-outcome-law]].

The conditional branch output is $\tau_a/p_a$ when $p_a>0$ and is $\bot$ when $p_a=0$, exactly as specified by [[def-qc-instrument-and-conditional-state]]. No normalized state is assigned to a zero-probability branch. A Kraus representation $\mathcal I_a(X)=\sum_jM_{a,j}XM_{a,j}^\dagger$ is only a representation of the observed branch map: $a$ is the outcome and $j$ is not an additional observed outcome.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space; the pairing is linear in its first argument ([[def-dimension]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Write $\mathcal L(H)$ for its complex-linear endomorphisms ([[def-vector-space-of-linear-maps]]) and let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty outcome set. A **finite POVM** on $H$ with outcomes $\Omega$ is a family $E=(E_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ with each $E_a$ nonnegative and $\sum_{a\in\Omega}E_a=I_H$; after any enumeration of $\Omega$, these operators form the finite complete positive family of [[def-qc-finite-positive-effect-family]]. Reordering does not alter the finite sum. The complete-family lemma [[lem-qc-complete-effect-family-members-are-effects]] shows that every $E_a$ also has nonnegative complement $I_H-E_a$, so each is an effect.

For a density operator $\rho$ on $H$ (a nonnegative operator of trace one, [[def-qc-density-operator]]), its **POVM outcome weights** are

$$p_\rho(a):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_a),\qquad a\in\Omega.$$

Here $\operatorname{tr}$ is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]).

The positivity and normalization of these weights are proved in [[thm-qc-povm-probabilities-normalize]]. A POVM specifies this outcome law; it does not by itself prescribe a conditional output state.

Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}$. If $0 \in S$ and $\sigma(n) \in S$ whenever $n \in S$, then $S = \mathbb{N}$. Equivalently (property form): if a property $P$ satisfies $P(0)$ and ($P(n) \Rightarrow P(\sigma(n))$) for all $n$, then $P(n)$ holds for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$. This is the induction principle, the basis of proof by induction.

derivations.claim: Give a finite history tree height $0$ when its root is a leaf; otherwise give it height one plus the maximum height of its finitely many child subtrees. For height $0$, there is a single empty history, no instrument is applied, and the leaf's terminal POVM is unchanged. Thus the branch-operator invariant holds at height $0$.

Let the root be internal and suppose the invariant holds for all trees of height at most $k$. For each root outcome $a$, [F2] replaces the root instrument and its edge unitary $S_{h,a}$ by a coherent record with the same unnormalized operator $Y_a$ on the child input and the reference, for every input operator $X$, while retaining a separate orthogonal label register $e_a$. Each child subtree has height at most $k$, so apply the induction hypothesis to its input operator $Y_a$ with the already retained history labels included in the finite reference. The operator need not be normalized or positive because the invariant is stated for every operator. The child constructions are controlled on the root's observed record; distinct labels occupy orthogonal record subspaces by [F1]–[F2], so the continuations preserve each full-history branch separately and do not merge histories.

By finite induction [F5] from step 1.1 and the preservation argument in step 2.1, every finite history tree has equal measured and coherently deferred unnormalized branch operators for each complete history and every finite reference.

For a leaf history $h$ and terminal outcome $z$, apply the same effect $F_z^h\otimes I_R$ to the equal branch operators from step 3.1 and take traces. This gives equal joint probabilities. The preterminal data-reference outputs conditioned on history $h$ agree after dividing their equal branch operators by the common positive history probability; zero-probability branches are never normalized by [F3]. Equality of the operators for arbitrary $R$ preserves reference correlations. Any required dilation and block controls remain explicit operation-model costs as stated.

Let $C=\mathbb C^2$ be a control qubit with ordered orthonormal basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$, let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, and let $U:H\to H$ be unitary. On the control-first register $C\otimes H$, define

$$C(U):=\begin{pmatrix}I_H&0\\0&U\end{pmatrix}.$$

Thus $C(U)(|0\rangle\otimes v)=|0\rangle\otimes v$ and $C(U)(|1\rangle\otimes v)=|1\rangle\otimes Uv$. **Controlled access** means that the chosen operation model explicitly grants a call to this block operator. An ordinary call to a black-box $U$ does not silently grant a controlled call, and no query or gate cost is assigned unless the model states it.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty outcome set ([[def-dimension]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Its **endomorphisms** are its complex-linear maps $H\to H$ ([[def-vector-space-of-linear-maps]]); for an endomorphism $P$, $P^*$ denotes its adjoint, which exists uniquely in finite dimension ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]]). A **finite projective measurement** on $H$ with outcomes $\Omega$ is a family $(P_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ of endomorphisms such that

$$P_a^*=P_a,\qquad P_a^2=P_a,\qquad P_aP_b=0\ (a\ne b),\qquad \sum_{a\in\Omega}P_a=I_H.$$

The products above are compositions, the sum is pointwise addition of endomorphisms, and $I_H$ is the identity map; these operations preserve linear maps ([[prop-linear-maps-form-a-vector-space]], [[lem-composition-and-identity-linear-maps]]). The projections $P_a=0$ are permitted. For a density operator $\rho$ on $H$ (nonnegative and trace one, [[def-qc-density-operator]]), the associated outcome weights are $p_\rho(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$; their nonnegativity and normalization are proved in [[thm-qc-projective-measurement-outcome-law]].

Let $\rho$ be a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$, and let $(P_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ be a finite projective measurement on $H$. Then $p_\rho(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$ lies in $[0,1]$ for every $a$, and $\sum_{a\in\Omega}p_\rho(a)=1$.

Let $\rho$ be a density operator and $(P_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ a finite projective measurement on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$. Put $p_a=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$. If $p_a>0$, then

$$\rho_a:=\frac{P_a\rho P_a}{p_a}$$

is a density operator whose image $\operatorname{im}(\rho_a):=\{\rho_a x:x\in H\}$ is contained in $\operatorname{im}(P_a)$ ([[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]). This statement assigns a conditional state only on positive-probability branches.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. Two nonzero vectors $x,y\in H$ represent the same **ray** when $y=\alpha x$ for some nonzero $\alpha\in\mathbb C$. A **pure state** is such a ray. If $u$ is a unit representative, its associated operator is $P_u=|u\rangle\langle u|$, with the bra, ket and outer-product convention of [[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]]. The theorem [[thm-qc-ray-projector-well-defined-and-bijective]] proves that this operator is a rank-one orthogonal projection independent of the chosen unit representative, so it is the operator representative of the pure state.

All complex inner products in this track use the root convention: they are
linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). For vectors $x,y$ in the same
space, define the Dirac pairing by

$$\langle x|y\rangle_D:=\langle y,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}.$$

The ket $|x\rangle$ denotes the vector $x$. The bra $\langle x|$ denotes the
linear functional $z\mapsto\langle z,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}$.

For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H,K$, vectors $y\in H$ and
$x\in K$, define the rank-one linear map

$$|x\rangle\langle y|:H\to K,\qquad z\mapsto\langle z,y\rangle_{H,\mathrm{root}}x.$$

Given ordered orthonormal bases of $H$ and $K$, its coordinate matrix is
$[x][y]^\dagger$, where $[x]$ and $[y]$ are the corresponding coordinate
columns and $M^\dagger:=\overline M^{\mathsf T}$ is the conjugate transpose.
The coordinate assertion is established in
[[thm-qc-dirac-notation-coordinate-identity]].

For nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product $H$, the map sending a ray $[u]$ to the rank-one projector $P_u=|u\rangle\langle u|$ of any unit representative is well-defined and bijective onto the rank-one orthogonal projections on $H$. Each $P_u$ is non-negative and has trace one.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root library's convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. A **density operator** on $H$ is a non-negative endomorphism $\rho:H\to H$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=1$; non-negative and trace have the meanings of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]] and [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. The zero-dimensional space is excluded: its only endomorphism has trace $0$.

Here $\ker\rho=\{x\in H:\rho x=0\}$, using the kernel of a linear map from [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **support** of $\rho$ is the orthogonal complement of its kernel in the root convention:

$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho):=\{x\in H: \langle x,y\rangle=0\text{ for every }y\in\ker\rho\}.$$

For a subspace $S\subseteq H$, $\rho$ is **faithful on $S$** when $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)=S$ and the restriction $\rho|_S:S\to S$ is positive definite in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. This restriction is an endomorphism: if $x\in S$ and $y\in\ker\rho$, self-adjointness gives $\langle\rho x,y\rangle=\langle x,\rho y\rangle=0$, so $\rho x\in(\ker\rho)^\perp=S$.

For a gate occurrence $g=(\gamma,w)$ in a circuit on $\mathcal Q_n$, let $\widetilde U_g$ be the global embedding from [[lem-qc-local-gate-wire-embedding]]. For a layer $L_t=(g_1,\ldots,g_s)$, define
$$U_{L_t}:=\widetilde U_{g_s}\cdots\widetilde U_{g_1}.$$
For a circuit with chronological layers $L_1,\ldots,L_d$, define
$$U_C:=U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}.$$
The empty circuit and every empty layer denote the identity on $\mathcal Q_n$.

For an integer $d\ge 1$, the $d$-level register is the complex inner-product
space $Q_d=\mathbb C^d$ with the standard pairing
$\langle z,w\rangle_{\rm root}=\sum_{j<d}z_j\overline{w_j}$, linear in the
first argument as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]] and
[[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]. Its **computational basis** is the
ordered standard basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of [[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]].
The register's alphabet is the ordered set $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$.

For $n\ge0$, the $n$-qubit register is the ordered tensor product over
$\mathbb C$ of $n$ copies of $Q_2$. Here $\otimes_{\mathbb C}$ is the algebraic
module tensor product ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),
with its complex-module structure and finite iterated/empty-product conventions
from [[thm-commutative-ring-module-structure-on-a-tensor-product]] and
[[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]. The tuple of
bit positions is ordered lexicographically, with the first wire as the most
significant position; the product-basis theorem below establishes the
corresponding elementary tensors as a basis. For $n=0$, the empty tensor
product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. This one-dimensional trivial
register is distinct from the zero vector space $\mathbb C^0$. By definition a
register has positive dimension; a zero-dimensional space may still occur as a
factor in the more general tensor-space construction below.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

By the matrix $H$ in Given and the circuit semantics [F7], applying $H$ to the first qubit sends the initial vector to $u=(|00\rangle+|10\rangle)/\sqrt2$. The basis in [F8] is orthonormal, so $\|u\|=1$; [F5]–[F6] therefore give the input density $\rho=|u\rangle\langle u|$.

The matrix of $\rho$ in [F8] has diagonal $(1/2,0,1/2,0)$ and nonzero off-diagonal entries only in positions $(00,10)$ and $(10,00)$, each $1/2$. Applying the diagonal projectors gives terminal weights $1/2$ on $00,11$ and zero on $01,10$ by [F3]. Thus the coherent circuit has the same joint law.

By [F4], the normalized conditional states are $P_0\rho P_0/(1/2)=|00\rangle\langle00|$ and $P_1\rho P_1/(1/2)=|10\rangle\langle10|$. On the outcome-$0$ branch the target is unchanged; on the outcome-$1$ branch the matrix $X$ in Given sends $|10\rangle$ to $|11\rangle$. The measured-and-controlled circuit therefore has the joint law stated.

The displayed branches are the one-instrument, one-bit case of the coherent equivalence in [thm-qc-deferred-measurement]. The measurement label stays the first wire and the target update depends on that label.
